payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket visibly closed more than in the input image, with its front panels brought together at least in part?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the jacket's front panels brought together along some portion of the closure compared with the input. Fail if the jacket is visibly unchanged or more open. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed from the image or comparison evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Assess only the woman's jacket identified in the input image; judge visible change to its front closure, not unrelated edits.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node’s binding and question capture the requested end state, but the trace’s “absent” conclusion is not well supported by the supplied images: the edited jacket is turned and swinging outward, so its apparent opening may reflect pose/motion rather than a reliable comparison of closure. Keep the full-closure criterion, but make the checks distinguish the jacket’s actual front closure from a panel displaced by movement, and compare corresponding visible regions in source and edit. The rubric permits “partial” only when evidence establishes progress; do not infer progress or absence from a single ambiguous view. If the closure cannot be assessed because of pose, occlusion, or image ambiguity, preserve that uncertainty as unknown rather than converting it to fail. The checks are valid and executed with high confidence, so this is not a transport/schema failure; investigate whether their evidence and confidence are calibrated to the visual ambiguity. The reference label constrains the aggregate only and does not establish which individual check or criterion is wrong.
s2: The endpoint criterion is appropriate; improve the binding/evidence guidance rather than relaxing full closure. The edited image shows the woman turned sideways with the jacket swinging outward, so the visible gap alone does not reliably establish that the closure remains open. Require assessment of the actual closure line using corresponding visible regions in source and edit, distinguishing a displaced panel from separated front panels. If pose or occlusion prevents that distinction, return unknown instead of a confident fail; calibrate confidence to this ambiguity. Keep partial progress separate from complete fulfillment and only infer progress when the images support it. The checks executed validly, so this is a visual-evidence/calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure; the aggregate reference does not identify which individual criterion is wrong.
